title: How Much Fiber in Popcorn? 3.6g per 3 Cups
description: Popcorn: about 3.6 g of fiber per 3 cups, air-popped (13% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in popcorn?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Snacks, popcorn, air-popped (Unsalted)

intro: Popcorn ranks #5 of 8 grains on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in popcorn by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in popcorn?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists snacks, popcorn, air-popped (unsalted) at 15.1 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (3 cups, air-popped; 24 g) therefore has about 3.6 g of fiber and 92 calories. That is 13% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 14% of a 25 g day and 10% of a 38 g day.

Popcorn is a whole grain, and because air-popped popcorn is mostly air, a big bowl is low in calories for the fiber it provides. Three cups is a common snack portion and lands in the same range as a slice or two of whole wheat bread.

sections.heading: Air-popped vs microwave vs movie popcorn
paragraphs: The figures here are for plain air-popped popcorn. Oil and butter add calories but not fiber, so microwave and theater popcorn have similar fiber per cup with far more calories.
Popcorn volume is hard to measure consistently. If you have a kitchen scale, weigh it: about 8 g per cup is USDA’s reference.

sections.heading: How popcorn compares with other grains
paragraphs: Of the 8 grains on this site, popcorn ranks #5 for fiber per typical serving and #3 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 4 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [brown rice](/fiber-in-brown-rice) at 3.2 g (1 cup, cooked); [wheat bran](/fiber-in-wheat-bran) at 3.1 g (2 tbsp); [quinoa](/fiber-in-quinoa) at 5.2 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), popcorn is #31 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding popcorn to your day
paragraphs: Pop a quarter cup of kernels (which makes several cups popped) and season with a little salt, chili, or nutritional yeast. Pair with a piece of fruit for a 6–8 g snack.

Example: 3 cups popcorn, 1 apple. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 8 g of fiber, with 3.6 g from the popcorn. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of popcorn?
faqs.a: 15.1 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Snacks, popcorn, air-popped (Unsalted)). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in popcorn (1 cup, air-popped)?
faqs.a: About 1.2 g, for 8 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Yes. Popcorn is a whole-grain corn kernel. The Whole Grains Council and U.S. Dietary Guidelines both count it as a whole grain.

faqs.q: Is popcorn high in fiber per calorie?
faqs.a: Plain air-popped popcorn is one of the higher-fiber snacks per calorie, about 4 g per 100 kcal. Oil and butter lower that ratio quickly.
